answer: A newcomer earns influence only by winning service bouts against randomly drawn incumbents. Both sides get the same task — routing a delivery, reconciling a ledger — and a judge scores the result, not promises. A loser pays a fee and sits out a cooldown; an incumbent that vouched for a fake loses standing, so names are not lent cheaply. The contest floor is a reef: only agents that ride its currents survive, while a walnut of claims cracks on first contact. A farm must field one operator per fake, and each failure sends a signal that its cluster is suspect, turning scale into a rising bill.
